independence_evidence: Site footer states 'The Dorchester Review is published by the Foundation for Civic Literacy', a small Ottawa foundation with its own chairman and advisory board; run by part-time editors, no media-group ownership.
qualifies_reason: Independent foundation-published Canadian quarterly of historical commentary whose Summer 2026 print edition is the current single copy on sale.
what_it_is: A Canadian journal of historical commentary and book reviews, with long essays on Canadian and British history, biography, politics and culture written from a conservative, polemical standpoint. Each quarterly print edition runs reviews and features on subjects such as Louis Riel, residential schools, the Senate and literary policy, with a mix of academics, former political staffers and journalists as contributors. It suits readers interested in Canadian history and conservative political argument who want a print review rather than a daily news outlet.
